title: An object of the derived category has a left dual precisely when it is perfect, and the dual is the dual of a perfect complex
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises the perfect objects of D(R) as exactly those admitting a left dual, and identifies that dual with the object M^vee of the dual-perfect-complex lemma (source lines 38580-38591). One direction is structural: a bounded complex of finite projective modules has a left dual already in the category of complexes (proof lines 38594-38598). The converse is the hard direction and occupies the rest of the proof. From a left dual (N, eta, epsilon) one chooses a representative M^bullet and a K-flat complex N^bullet with flat terms, writes eta(1) as a finite sum of tensors m_{n,i} tensor n_{-n,i}, and builds the subcomplex K^bullet generated by the m_{n,i} and their differentials (proof lines 38601-38622). The key move is that eta factors through K tensor^L N and the identity on M therefore factors through K, which forces M to lie in D^-(R) (proof lines 38623-38641). One then re-represents M by a bounded above complex of free modules, uses the same finite-sum expression to cut out a bounded subcomplex K^bullet consisting of finite free modules, and again factors the identity through K; since K is perfect and a summand of M, M is perfect (proof lines 38642-38653). The non-routine content is the factoring-of-the-identity trick applied twice, once to bound M above and once to bound it below.
